messages:
Laura Chen: Quick question — can a k8s ServiceAccount have multiple IRSA IAM roles attached via annotations? Thinking about a pod that needs both S3 read and Dynamo write access. :thinking:
Ajay Patel: Not directly. IRSA maps a KSA to one IAM role via the annotation eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn.
Marcos Rivera: Yep, single role. You can either create separate service accounts per permission set, or use role chaining inside the app (STS AssumeRole).
Rachael Kim: Another option: give the KSA a role that can assume other roles (sts:AssumeRole) and then call STS from the pod to switch to secondary role when needed.
Ajay Patel: Example KSA annotation:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: foo
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-app-role
```
Marcos Rivera: Terraform snippet (IRSA resource):
```
resource "aws_iam_role" "app" {
  name = "redwood-app-role"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume_role_policy.json
}

resource "kubernetes_service_account" "app_sa" {
  metadata {
    name = "app-sa"
    namespace = kubernetes_namespace.foo.metadata[0].name
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.app.arn
    }
  }
}
```
Laura Chen: If we go with STS chaining, we need to ensure the initial role has sts:AssumeRole on the secondary ones, and audit that in console.
Rachael Kim: Also watch token expiration. The IRSA token is short-lived; your app needs to handle refresh and caching of assumed creds.
infra-bot: doc: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html
Ajay Patel: TL;DR: pick 1) multiple SA per permission or 2) single SA that assumes other roles at runtime. For cross-account roles, the assume-role pattern is standard.
Laura Chen: Thanks — I'll prototype a two-SA approach first and post a PR. Ping me if you want to review the helm changes.
Marcos Rivera: happy to review. :thumbsup:
